name: moj-analytical-services/splink
what: Probabilistic record linkage (Fellegi-Sunter, EM training) on SQL backends incl. DuckDB.
why_it_matters: Our identity pass step 2 (Splink on name+dates+co-occurrence for the non-hard-key remainder) and the EM ~1M records/min on a laptop claim in SYSTEM.md section 2. Runs on DuckDB, which matches the Parquet lake plan.
note: use: core matcher for the identity pass; MIT; DuckDB backend fits the lake; keep hard keys (QID/ORCID/ISNI) ahead of it.

name: opensanctions/nomenklatura
what: Framework to de-duplicate and integrate FollowTheMoney entity streams; statement store and judgement (same/different) model.
why_it_matters: The judgement graph in SYSTEM.md section 2 (left_ref, right_ref, verdict same|different|unsure, by, reason) and the statement-with-source store come from this design. Its 'different' judgements are the reversible-merge mechanism we want.
note: use: copy the judgement and statement pattern; MIT; low stars but the design is the closest prior art to our table set. Consider FtM as export schema.

name: opensanctions/yente
what: Search and bulk-matching API over FollowTheMoney datasets, with the Reconciliation API spec.
why_it_matters: Shows how to serve identity matching as an API and speak the OpenRefine/Reconciliation protocol, which would let Mix'n'match-style review and bulk matching plug in. Not needed as a server for us; the pattern is what matters.
ui_notes: Reconciliation API compatibility lets OpenRefine act as a review UI for ambiguous matches.
note: borrow-idea: reconciliation endpoint for the review queue; do not run it as a service.

name: apple/embedding-atlas
what: Interactive visualisation, cross-filter and search for large embedding sets.
why_it_matters: Could inspect utterance vectors in said.sqlite (sqlite-vec) and check dedup clusters and speaker-attribution clusters visually before they reach advisors.
ui_notes: Use as an internal QA view of utterance embeddings and MinHash/SimHash dedup clusters, not a public page.
note: borrow-idea: internal QA tool for embeddings and dedup clusters; not on the serving path.

name: jacomyal/sigma.js
what: WebGL renderer for graphs of thousands of nodes and edges.
why_it_matters: Renders a person's 1-hop and 2-hop neighbourhood (SYSTEM.md section 6 serving uses precomputed neighbours in static JSON). Pairs with graphology for the data layer.
ui_notes: Neighbourhood view on each person page, built from the static JSON per T2/T3 person; keep the graph small (depth 2) so WebGL is not needed for most pages.
note: borrow-idea: neighbourhood widget on person pages; MIT; render only 1-2 hops to stay light.

name: yt-dlp/yt-dlp
what: Command-line downloader for video and audio from YouTube and hundreds of sites; channel and playlist metadata listing.
why_it_matters: The one-off channel inventory (every video as metadata) and captions for T3-picked videos in SYSTEM.md section 4. Metadata-only listing is the cheap path.
note: use: metadata and caption fetch for the channel inventory; Unlicense; check the platform terms before bulk download, and never keep audio beyond ASR.

name: m-bain/whisperX
what: Whisper ASR with forced-alignment word timestamps and pyannote-based diarization.
why_it_matters: Word-level timing is needed for the utterance span field (char/time offsets) and for attributing words to a speaker turn. Also the reference pipeline for ASR plus diarization.
note: borrow-idea: the word-alignment step is what we want; the diarization step depends on gated pyannote models, so keep the pipeline swappable.

name: ggml-org/whisper.cpp
what: C/C++ port of Whisper for CPU and Apple Silicon (Metal) inference, with quantised models.
why_it_matters: Batch ASR for the Mac mini without a Python stack; this is the local ASR engine for T3 transcripts on Apple Silicon.
note: use: local batch ASR on the mini (Metal); MIT; no Python dependency.

name: SYSTRAN/faster-whisper
what: Whisper reimplementation on CTranslate2 with int8 quantisation and VAD filtering.
why_it_matters: Fast Python-side batch ASR for long audio back-fills (Elon-scale, ~500 h audio in SYSTEM.md section 1 cost estimate). Outputs segment timestamps directly.
note: use: batch ASR when a Python pipeline is simpler than whisper.cpp; MIT; pick one of the two engines, not both.

name: ekzhu/datasketch
what: MinHash, weighted MinHash, LSH and LSH Forest, HyperLogLog, and HNSW in Python.
why_it_matters: Utterance near-duplicate detection (5-gram MinHash, Jaccard ~0.8) in SYSTEM.md section 4, dedup level 2. Also MinHash-LSH blocking for the identity pass.
note: use: MinHash-LSH for utterance dedup and blocking; MIT; SimHash for short posts is a separate step.

name: StanfordHCI/genagents
what: Generative agents built from qualitative interview transcripts (1,000-person study); memory, reflection and survey-response code. The joonspk-research/genagents URL redirects here.
why_it_matters: Closest published pattern to a quote-only advisor: an agent built from a person's own interview text, answering with grounded responses. Also its restricted-access split (aggregate open, individual gated) is a model for consent on T3 people.
ui_notes: Memory and reflection pattern can inform the advisor's retrieval step; the sample agent is a demo.
note: borrow-idea: interview-to-agent pattern for the advisor; last push Nov 2024; the 1,000-person bank is restricted, not in the repo.

name: k2-fsa/sherpa-onnx
what: On-device speech stack on onnxruntime: ASR, speaker diarization, speaker identification and verification, VAD, TTS.
why_it_matters: The only single toolkit in the shortlist that does ASR, diarization and speaker ID (enrolment and verification) offline. Covers SYSTEM.md section 4 speaker attribution (voiceprint from a known-solo clip) in one dependency.
note: use: ASR plus diarization plus speaker-ID on the mini; Apache-2.0; pushed today; check each model's own licence before use.

name: pyannote/pyannote-audio
what: Neural speaker diarization toolkit: speech activity, speaker change and overlap detection, speaker embedding; pretrained pipelines on Hugging Face.
why_it_matters: SYSTEM.md section 4 names pyannote turns as step 2 of speaker attribution. Turns plus a voiceprint give the attribution method and confidence stored per utterance.
note: use: diarization turns for attribution; code is MIT but pretrained pipelines are gated on Hugging Face and carry their own model licences (not checked here).

name: MahmoudAshraf97/whisper-diarization
what: Pipeline: Whisper ASR, forced alignment, speaker diarization, with punctuation restore.
why_it_matters: Ready-made pipeline that outputs speaker-labelled, time-stamped transcripts, the format we need before utterance rows.
note: borrow-idea: a reference for stitching ASR, alignment and diarization; we would rather build on sherpa-onnx or whisperX directly.

name: modelscope/3D-Speaker
what: Speaker verification, recognition and diarization toolkit with ERes2Net, CAM++ and ECAPA-TDNN embeddings.
why_it_matters: Voiceprint embeddings for enrolling a known speaker from a solo clip, then matching utterances (SYSTEM.md section 4 step 2).
note: borrow-idea: strong embeddings for voiceprint attribution; Apache-2.0; last push Dec 2025; sherpa-onnx covers the same need in one dependency.

name: modelscope/FunASR
what: ASR toolkit with VAD, punctuation, speaker diarization pipelines and streaming.
why_it_matters: Alternative ASR plus diarization stack with good multilingual coverage (50+ languages in its models), relevant for non-English speakers in the corpus.
note: borrow-idea: second opinion for multilingual ASR; MIT; keep as fallback, not the default.

name: dedupeio/dedupe
what: Python fuzzy matching and entity resolution with active learning from labelled pairs.
why_it_matters: Its active-learning loop (ask the human only about the most uncertain pairs) is the pattern for our review queue in the identity band. Last push July 2025.
ui_notes: Active-learning pair review is the model for the yes/no/unsure queue that Haiku checkers can clear.
note: borrow-idea: take the active-learning pair-review loop; Splink does the matching; no need to run dedupe itself.

name: gramps-project/gramps
what: Desktop genealogy program: people, families, events, places, sources and citations as a data model.
why_it_matters: Its event, citation and place model is a mature prosopography schema for birth/death/marriage facts with sources, which matches our statement-with-source table and qualifiers (start, end, place).
note: borrow-idea: study the citation and event model only; GPL-2.0 means no code copied into our repo.

name: gramps-project/gramps-web
what: Web front end and API for Gramps family trees.
why_it_matters: Shows a person-page and relationship-navigation UI over a genealogy DB. Reference for serving layout only.
ui_notes: Person page with family and relationship navigation; reference only.
note: skip: AGPL-3.0 (network copyleft) makes reuse risky; look at the UI, do not vendor it.

name: timhutton/twitter-archive-parser
what: Parses an X/Twitter data-export archive (tweets, media, replies) into Markdown, HTML or JSON.
why_it_matters: Reference for reading the X archive export format (tweets.js wrapper, media, reply threads) that feeds the posts-as-utterances path for Elon-scale and other archives.
note: borrow-idea: copy the format knowledge, not the code; GPL-3.0; stale since Nov 2022, so re-check the export format.

name: jdepoix/youtube-transcript-api
what: Python client that fetches YouTube transcripts and auto-generated captions with start times.
why_it_matters: Caption fetch for T3-picked videos (SYSTEM.md section 1 and 4), segment-level timestamps for utterance spans. Avoids downloading audio.
note: use: captions for T3-picked videos; MIT; captions are auto-generated for many videos, so mark method and quality on the utterance.

name: pyannote/pyannote-metrics
what: Evaluation toolkit for diarization: DER, error breakdown and diagnostics.
why_it_matters: Needed to measure speaker-attribution accuracy on a hand-labelled sample before any voiceprint attribution reaches advisors (the 0.9 confidence gate in SYSTEM.md section 4).
note: use: DER evaluation for the attribution QA gate; MIT.

name: wq2012/awesome-diarization
what: Curated list of speaker-diarization papers, libraries, datasets and resources.
why_it_matters: Index of diarization options (libraries, datasets for evaluation) so we do not miss a newer model; saves search time.
note: borrow-idea: reading list for the diarization choice; not code.

name: narcotic-sh/senko
what: Fast speaker diarization tool.
why_it_matters: Candidate fast diarizer for long back-fills if pyannote is too slow on the mini.
note: borrow-idea: benchmark against pyannote on our sample; small community, MIT.

name: opentapioca/opentapioca
what: Entity linking of text mentions to Wikidata items, kept in step with Wikidata edits.
why_it_matters: Links person and org mentions in utterances and books to QIDs (the crosswalk key in SYSTEM.md section 2), which is the step after Wikidata itself.
note: borrow-idea: mention-to-QID linker for utterance speakers and cited people; check accuracy on our names before use.

name: WDscholia/scholia
what: Wikidata-driven scholarly profile pages (authors, papers, topics) built from SPARQL queries.
why_it_matters: A working person-page built from Wikidata plus works, close to our T1 person page layout.
ui_notes: Scholarly profile page: person header, works list, topic cloud. Reference for page layout.
note: borrow-idea: profile page layout and SPARQL patterns; GPL-3.0 so no code copied.

name: fisharebest/webtrees
what: Online genealogy application with GEDCOM import and export, and privacy rules for living people.
why_it_matters: Its living-person privacy rules and GEDCOM source-citation model are a useful check for our Life data (never publish living people's details).
note: borrow-idea: living-person privacy rule and GEDCOM interchange; GPL-3.0, read only.

name: geneweb/geneweb
what: Genealogy software with a web interface and a long-lived database format.
why_it_matters: Mature family-graph storage and relationship computation for large trees; a reference for graph-of-people at scale.
note: borrow-idea: relationship-computation ideas only; GPL-2.0.

name: OpenMOSS/MOSS-Transcribe-Diarize
what: 0.9B model for long-form transcription in 50+ languages with speaker diarization, timestamps and acoustic events.
why_it_matters: One model that does transcript plus speaker labels in a single pass; could cut the ASR-plus-diarization chain for long recordings.
note: borrow-idea: evaluate on a labelled clip against sherpa-onnx; Apache-2.0; new, so no track record yet.

name: ljsabc/Fujisaki
what: Prototype persona model built from a Twitter archive with LoRA fine-tuning on Alpaca-style data.
why_it_matters: Direct precedent for a persona from one person's posts. Fine-tuning a persona is the wrong layer for us; the quote-only advisor should retrieve, not imitate.
note: skip: 2023 prototype; fine-tuning imitates voice, against our quote-only rule; keep as a warning example.

name: zinggAI/zingg
what: Scalable ML entity resolution and master data management on Spark.
why_it_matters: Same job as Splink at larger scale on Spark. We do not run Spark on the mini, so it is not needed now.
note: skip: AGPL-3.0 and Spark-based; Splink covers our scale on DuckDB.

name: siznax/wptools
what: Python helper to pull infobox, Wikidata and links for a Wikipedia title.
why_it_matters: Convenience for single-person lookups, but we need bulk dump filtering, not per-title calls.
note: skip: stale since Aug 2023 and per-title; bulk Wikidata dump filter is the path.

name: Quantatirsk/AsrServe
what: Self-hosted ASR server with diarization and an OpenAI-compatible API.
why_it_matters: Would be a convenient ASR endpoint, but a server adds a moving part we do not need for batch work.
note: skip: no licence declared, so it cannot be used or vendored.

name: dariusk/twitter-archiver
what: Public searchable archive of one account's tweets.
why_it_matters: Presentation-only; no identity or ASR value for us.
note: skip: stale 2023 and presentation-only.
